local_checks.invariant: with_notice wraps instruction-file content in a per-call unforgeable random-tag boundary that content cannot imitate; the truncation marker sits inside the boundary; MCP and the built-in loop produce the same enclosure.
local_checks.result: with_notice draws tag=secrets.token_hex(8) and redraws while tag in text (instruction_files.py:132-134). Content containing the full NOTICE text plus a fake boundary with tag 'deadbeef' stayed strictly inside the real random-tag boundary, and the notice states a boundary line lacking the real tag is file text. The truncation marker is added before wrapping, so it is inside the boundary. Divergence: when the wrapped text exceeds agent.py _RESULT_LIMIT=20000, ToolClient.call_text truncates text[:20000]+marker (agent.py:126-127) and drops the closing boundary line, while mcp_server.read_file keeps it. No boundary failure results because the attacker cannot emit the random tag, so this is hardening.

local_checks.invariant: exec results carry a notice only (no boundary, by design); read classification uses the requested path; list_dir carries neither; reads through a link or non-instruction name are governed by the documented name-only limitation.
local_checks.result: service._run_tool sets res['notice'] for exec when paths_in_words hits (service.py:138-141) with no boundary, and call_text/MCP return exec/list_dir without with_notice, matching the design. read_file goes through IF.mark_read on the requested path with no link resolution, so reading an instruction file through a link (notes.md -> CLAUDE.md) yields no notice and would bypass a user read rule; this is the documented name-only limitation and is recorded as hardening (write side resolves links, read side does not).

x_hardening: agent.py ToolClient.call_text truncates the already-wrapped read result at _RESULT_LIMIT=20000 (agent.py:126-127), dropping the closing boundary line for large instruction files, while mcp_server.read_file keeps it; apply the length limit before with_notice wraps it.

Read classification does not resolve links (service._resolved only resolves write_file/delete_file), so reading an instruction file through a link yields no notice and could bypass a user read-block rule; resolving the read target as writes do would close the asymmetry.
escape_controls expands each control character to a 4-6 char escape; sinks that render attacker-sized strings through _shown should cap input length before escaping.

local_checks.invariant: The synchronous source-folder scan in create_sandbox must not starve the pool that serves agent tool calls, and its request-thread cost must be bounded; dispatch/pool separation holds.
local_checks.result: create_sandbox is a sync def human-only route (api.py:273-275, Depends(human_only)) running on the shared default Starlette/anyio threadpool, while tool calls run on a dedicated tool_pool ThreadPoolExecutor(32) via run_in_executor (api.py:175,317-320). So a slow scan cannot starve agent tool calls; it only occupies one default-threadpool slot shared with other human/admin routes. Scan cost is bounded by SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES=200_000 and the 10.0s deadline checked per entry inside the scandir iteration. Residual: a single blocking os.scandir()/next() on a slow or hung mount is not interrupted by the per-entry deadline, and the scan shares the default human-route threadpool; both reachable only via the human-only create route and bounded per request (hardening).

local_checks.invariant: scan reports complete=False whenever the list may be partial (hit cap, entry cap, unreadable dir), and the audit record keeps the count and truthfully marks a truncated list after bound_payload, which web.describe renders honestly.
local_checks.result: 201 instruction files -> scan returns exactly 200 hits with complete=False (0.018s). A lowered entry cap and an unreadable (chmod 0) subdir both yield complete=False while still returning the hits already found. _found_payload for 200 paths of 512 multibyte chars = 308661 bytes > AUDIT_PAYLOAD_MAX(131072): bound_payload sets payload_truncated=True and drops paths, but keeps count=200 and complete=False. web.describe then renders the count with '(목록이 길어 기록에서 잘림) (다 훑지 못함...)'. No 0-count or false-complete timeline row is possible.

x_hardening: create_sandbox (agentbox/api.py:273) is a synchronous handler, so IF.scan runs on Starlette's shared default anyio threadpool (distinct from tool_pool). A scan of an attacker-supplied source folder can hold one default-threadpool slot for up to the 10 s deadline; consider offloading the scan to a bounded dedicated executor.

instruction_files.scan (agentbox/instruction_files.py:160-193) checks SCAN_MAX_SECONDS only per scandir entry; a single os.scandir(d) open or the first next() on a slow/hung/FUSE/network mount is not interrupted by the deadline and would pin the request thread. Deployment-dependent and human-only; wrap the per-directory scandir in a watchdog or cancellable deadline.

_found_payload cuts each path with a character slice p[:512] (agentbox/service.py:783), so 200 multibyte paths (~308 KB) exceed AUDIT_PAYLOAD_MAX and force bound_payload to drop the whole list; count/complete survive. Enforcing FOUND_PATH_MAX in bytes would keep more paths.
